What degraded

  • The deck was scored SIXTEEN times. The rubric's new cap is five, and this run predates it. The round record is in runs/carousel/2026-08-25/RUN_RECORD.md.
  • Machine QA carries three soft warnings, none a failure: two on frame 4's greek field, which the craft judge verified by eye as grain rather than drawn marks, and one on frame 8's Laredo citation at worst-point contrast 4.2 against a 4.5 line.
  • The craft judge measured four type blocks under the deck's own 4.5 contrast floor that machine QA did not flag, because nothing in the engine solves the ground under a type box for its own contrast. Recorded as a proposal, not built.
  • Both dated public doors are state bodies in Austin. A reader in one of the fourteen places the deck names is handed nothing local to do, and the deck says so rather than inventing one.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Fifteen actions, and whether the instrument binds, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

1. The post copy

Four abatements never got a vote. The item they all stood on failed first.

That was March 10th in Brazoria County, first of fifteen actions by twelve Texas governments. Nine frames, all fifteen in order, sorted by whether the instrument binds.

Five took effect. San Angelo wrote three, allowing a data center only by conditional use and capping its cooling fill.

Five reached for a resolution. Not one is among the five that took effect.

On five more the record carries no date in force. Two were approvals, Wichita Falls and Williamson County.

Of eight items with a step still ahead, the two on a data center both sit with a state body. The nearer closes September 4th.

A Lubbock County commissioner was plain. "Resolutions do nothing, they are not binding." Is one worth passing?

#BrazoriaCounty #SanAngelo #FortWorth

The machine changed itself

  • The ship bar is 6.8 and the round cap is 5, both declared in config/carousel/scoring_rubric.yaml and read by run_complete.py rather than passed in.
    Your instruction, after this run scored one deck fifteen times across a night and shipped nothing. A bar with no bound on the search is a loop. A hard fail still stops the deck at any round, because a figure with no computation behind it or a quote that is not in its source is a factual gate and not a polish gate.
  • panel.py counts its own scoring rounds and writes the number into score.json.
    The cap makes that field the most valuable lie a run could tell, so the run does not get to write it. Every invocation appends a line and the round is the length of the file.
  • Two new gates, scripts/carousel/label_guard.py and quantifier_check.py, and gate_status.py now names the command that writes each report.
    port_audit was right that nothing ran them. label_guard asserts every label printed beside a claim id is the shape the record proves. quantifier_check reads every published surface from one list, which is the fix for repairs that land on the frame that was named and on no other surface.
  • qa.py splits the rule floor and adds a geometric x-height test.
    A rule struck through a line of type passed the old floor because the floor was in the wrong unit.

Each reverts on its own commit.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
